points.claim: Daenerys had stopped actively attacking when Jon stabbed her; the city had surrendered and no immediate threat existed.
points.support: The agreed record states that King's Landing had surrendered and organized resistance had ceased. Daenerys was not engaged in combat or threatening anyone at the moment of the killing.

points.claim: Jon lacked any formal authority to execute the queen; no council or law granted him that power.
points.support: The record shows Jon was not appointed by any governing body to act as judge or executioner. He was a former king and loyalist, not a legal authority.

points.claim: Jon did not seek any alternative to killing; he neither convened a council nor attempted detention or surrender of power.
points.support: The agreed record explicitly states that Jon had not convened a council, attempted detention, or sought a public surrender of power before the killing.

points.claim: Jon used his intimate relationship to get close enough to strike, showing premeditation rather than urgent necessity.
points.support: The record notes that Jon used their intimacy to approach Daenerys, indicating he planned the act in advance, not that he acted in immediate self-defense.

points.claim: The future harm Jon feared was speculative; Daenerys was not currently harming anyone, and other measures could have been taken to prevent her.
points.support: While Daenerys promised further campaigns, the record shows no imminent threat at the time of the killing. Safer alternatives, such as rallying allies or detaining her, were available.
